title: Extension of effective Cartier divisors across factorial local rings
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $V\subset X$ an open subscheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $D\subset V$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Suppose that for every $x\in X\setminus V$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a unique factorization domain: an integral domain in which every nonzero nonunit is a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and unit factors. Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor $D^{\mathrm{ext}}\subset X$ with $D^{\mathrm{ext}}\cap V=D$ as closed subschemes of $V$. No density, separatedness or integrality of $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: The open immersion $V\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. For an affine open $B\subset X$, $D\cap B$ is closed in the quasi-compact space $V\cap B$, so it is quasi-compact; hence $h:D\to X$ is quasi-compact. It is a monomorphism (a composite of the two subscheme inclusions), so its diagonal is an isomorphism and it is quasi-separated as well. Form its scheme-theoretic image $C\subset X$ using [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] its restriction to $V$ is the scheme-theoretic image of the closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow V$, which is $D$ by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion]. Thus $C\cap V=D$ as closed subschemes.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor, proof; construction of the scheme-theoretic image and restriction to opens

proof.text: Fix $x\in X\setminus V$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$. Its coordinate ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], so $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is a UFD by the hypothesis. The canonical morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is flat and identifies the closed-point local ring with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Therefore [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change] identifies $C_A=C\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the scheme-theoretic image of $E=D\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A$. Set $W=c^{-1}V$. The local equations of $D$ remain nonzerodivisors after pullback: every stalk map of $c$ is an isomorphism by the same canonical-morphism lemma. Thus $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $W$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor, proof; reduction to the spectrum of the local UFD at a complement point

proof.text: The single affine chart makes $\operatorname{Spec}A$ locally Noetherian. It is quasi-compact: a cover can be refined to basic opens $D(b)$, the $b$ generate the unit ideal (otherwise a maximal ideal misses the cover), and a finite expression for $1$ yields a finite subcover. Thus it is Noetherian, and its open $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Its local rings are prime localizations of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], hence UFDs by [lem-sfb-ufd-prime-localizations]. Apply [lem-sfb-factorial-cartier-prime-decomposition] to obtain $\mathcal I_E=\prod_i\mathcal I_{E_i}^{a_i}$ with integral Cartier components having generic points $\xi_i$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{W,\xi_i}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor, proof; finite decomposition into integral effective Cartier divisors

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p_i\subset A$ correspond to $\xi_i$. Since $W$ is open, its local ring there is $A_{\mathfrak p_i}$; the dimension-one conclusion says that $\mathfrak p_i$ has height one. By [lem-trf-ufd-height-one], $\mathfrak p_i=(f_i)$. Choose the $f_i$ pairwise nonassociated; each is a nonzero prime element because $A$ is a domain and $(f_i)$ is a nonzero prime ideal. The reduced closed subscheme $V(f_i)\cap W$ is precisely $E_i$: both are the reduced closure in $W$ of $\xi_i$. Indeed on every affine chart meeting that closure the defining radical prime is the prime corresponding to that generic point. Hence the given equality of ideal products says that $E$ is cut out on $W$ by $F=\prod_i f_i^{a_i}$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor, proof; height-one primes are principal; the equation for the divisor on the open

proof.text: Write $J\subset A$ for the ideal of $C_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel], $J=\ker(A\to\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E))$. The equation in the preceding step gives $(F)\subset J$. Conversely, take $b\in J$. For each $i$ choose a basic open $D(h_i)\subset W$ containing $\xi_i$, so $h_i\notin(f_i)$. Its restriction satisfies $b/1\in(F)A_{h_i}\subset(f_i^{a_i})A_{h_i}$. The fraction equality rule gives $h_i^n b\in(f_i^{a_i})$ for some $n$. Since the prime $f_i$ does not divide $h_i$, unique factorization implies $f_i^{a_i}\mid b$. The $f_i$ are pairwise nonassociated, so unique factorization gives $F\mid b$. Thus $J=(F)$. If the decomposition is empty, $E$ is empty, $F=1$, and the same kernel is $A$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor, proof; explicit verification that the closure ideal is the product ideal

proof.text: The product $F$ is nonzero in the domain $A$ (including the empty product $1$), so multiplication by $F$ is injective. At the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, its ideal $J=(F)$ is already the stalk ideal. The canonical-morphism identification in step 2 therefore proves that $\mathcal I_{C,x}$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor. For $x\in V$ this follows from $C\cap V=D$; at points outside $C$ the generator is $1$. Every stalk of $\mathcal I_C$ is now covered. Apply [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading] to the closed subscheme $C$ of the locally Noetherian $X$. It is an effective Cartier divisor, and the previously proved equality $C\cap V=D$ gives the required $D^{\mathrm{ext}}=C$.
